  1827 events (95% of all), mu 3161.6 eV, sigma 237.2 eV (7.50%)

left out: PDS2 (acceptance 42%)
  all 11 channels, 797 events (41%): mu 3262.6 eV, sigma 261.4 eV (8.01%), = 31.46%
  bias: on that subsample the core sum is 3008.3 eV against 3161.6 eV over all events (-4.8%), so requiring those channels to fit selects events that put less energy in the core.
  their share on that subsample is 3262.6 - 3008.3 = 254.2 eV.

The full efficiency is therefore a bracket, not a single number:
  lower  31.46%  (3262.6 eV): the all-channel sum taken as it stands. Reads low if that subsample is not representative, and it is not: its core sum is -4.8% off.
  upper  32.94%  (3415.8 eV): the unbiased core sum plus that share. Reads high because a subsample whose core is low has its energy sitting closer to the left-out channel, so 254.2 eV overstates the typical share.
  => collection efficiency = 32 +- 1 %, and the way to collapse the bracket is to make PDS2 fittable (its low-frequency artefact is what fails the NRMSE cut), not more statistics.
